title: LH-Mix: Local Hierarchy Correlation Guided Mixup over Hierarchical Prompt Tuning

problem.claim: Hierarchical text classification assigns one or more labels from a hierarchy to each text.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often model local hierarchies as sequences and ignore implicit correlations among sibling or peer relationships.

contributions.claim: The paper integrates local hierarchies into a manual depth-level prompt to capture parent-child relationships.
The paper applies Mixup to hierarchical prompt tuning to improve latent correlations among sibling or peer relationships.
The paper proposes a Mixup ratio guided by local hierarchy correlation to capture intrinsic correlations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the local-hierarchy-correlation-guided Mixup ratio as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the LH-Mix model demonstrates remarkable performance across three widely used datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper addresses hierarchical text classification.
Global hierarchy representations can produce redundant graph structures, motivating text-specific local hierarchies.
Existing local-hierarchy methods emphasize explicit parent-child sequences while overlooking implicit sibling or peer correlations.
LH-Mix combines manual depth-level hierarchical prompts with Mixup and a local-correlation-guided Mixup ratio.
The authors report strong performance across three widely used datasets.

source_observation.claim: Local hierarchy modeling should account for both parent-child structure and sibling or peer correlations.

interpretation.claim: Representing hierarchical relationships solely as explicit sequences may miss useful relational information.

application.claim: For hierarchical classification systems, combine hierarchy-aware prompting with mechanisms that model local peer correlations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets or task setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the manual depth-level prompt or the Mixup-ratio formulation in detail.
